They kind of created their own genre. It’s not quite walking sim, not quite puzzle game. That said, for inventing the Telltale genre, they never really found it so to speak. Every game struggled to find a gameplay element that justified an interactive choose your own adventure. Their best successes came from those games with strong story elements (TWD) and strong licenses (Minecraft). As time went on it became clear that these two elements were really all they were ever going to have.

I’ve been a fan of most of their games from the beginning, simply because I like gaming to be a way to unwind at the end of a rough day. If I want to get a new skill, I’ll pick up something practical before I dedicate every evening to an online pvp. That said, I could see the cracks developing towards the end. Their later games were more formulaic. For example, the facade of choices that matter goes out the window when once you’re given a choice to save a character’ life, that character then has no dialogue of importance for the rest of the episode and is killed off immediately in the folllowing episode. The linear tracks are suddenly visible and the game doesn’t even feel like a choose your own adventure any more. Also, the focus on puzzle elements and QuickTime events just faded over time. Earlier games that focused on each (Back to the Future and Jurassic Park respectively) stand in stark difference from later games. TWD season 2, for example, featured a “puzzle” where you turn off a windmill by opening he control box and press the off button.

As for the SJW shit, I wasn’t really aware of it. I haven’t played their most recent games, but their games as of a couple years ago didn’t have much of any political messaging in them.
